title: Assurance readiness & access review - Mantle Finance
summary: Redwood team walked Mantle Finance through SOC 2 / ISO 27001 artifacts access, RBAC/SSO options for private deployments, KMS integration patterns, and audit log retention. Customer emphasized data residency for EU customers, strict key management with customer-managed KMS, and wanting read-only access to reports. Agreed next steps: share recent SOC 2 Type II report, map controls against Mantle inventory, and set up pilot with RBAC role matrix and test KMS integration in staging.
topics: Private deployment (VPC) options and evidence flow

Riley Patel - Prepare controls mapping template (Redwood controls -> Mantle control IDs) and upload to shared drive - due 2027-03-09

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-04 15:00 UTC | Duration: 65 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Chen (Redwood AE), Riley Patel (Redwood SE), Alex Romano (Mantle CISO), Priya Desai (Head of Security), Mark Liu (SRE), Sana Kaur (Compliance)

Summary (auto-generated may be noisy): quick run through of controls and access, customer wants KMS separated, uh hm, also wants logs retained in EU, and RBAC mapped to their internal roles.

[00:00] Jamie: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, hi Alex, Priya, Mark, Sana?
[00:08] Alex: Yep, Alex here. Thanks.
[00:10] Priya: Priya here.
[00:12] Mark: Mark on the line.
[00:14] Sana: Sana.
[00:16] Jamie: Great. So agenda — we're going to walk through our SOC 2 material, how you can access the reports, and then Riley will go through RBAC/SSO and KMS flows. We'll leave time for your questions and then recap next steps.

[00:36] Riley: Hi all. quick note on terminology, sometimes our docs say Redwood Dedicated, other times they say Redwood Private; they're often used in the transcript as interchangeable. If you see "Redwood Private" that's the VPC/on-prem package.

[00:50] Priya: The main ask from compliance is: we need to see the latest SOC 2 Type II evidence, and we need a controls mapping to our ISO inventory. We also need to confirm keys are customer-managed HSM or KMS, and audit logs stay in EU for EU tenants.

[01:10] Jamie: Totally understood. We can share a sanitized SOC 2 Type II and an ISO annex. For trust-center access, we support read-only views for your auditors, and we can export PDFs of the reports.

[01:28] Alex: When you say read-only, is that a console account with RBAC or a separate portal link? We have strict rule: auditors should not need active credentials if possible.

[01:40] Riley: Good question. We have two main approaches: 1) Trust portal — a read-only workspace that you can invite auditors to (SAML SSO supported, scoped roles) or 2) ephemeral signed S3 links for specific artifacts. Both are commonly used. The trust portal keeps an audit trail for who accessed what.

[01:58] Mark: Are those access events logged to your audit logs? We need the access events exported to our SIEM.

[02:06] Riley: Yes — access events generate audit records. We can ship logs to a customer-managed destination: S3 with KMS encryption, or a syslog/forwarder depending on setup. Note: we sometimes see transcriptions list the KV cache stuff weirdly, but it's K V cache, not cash, ha.

[02:28] Sana: Ok, KMS — we require CMK (customer managed keys) in our cloud accounts, ideally HSM backed. Do you support that?

[02:36] Jamie: Yes. For private deployments and dedicated customers we support customer-managed KMS keys (KMS CMKs) and can enable HSM provisioning. There's an integration pattern for bring-your-own-key where the key is never exported from your account.

[02:54] Alex: Is key rotation automated? We have strict rotation policies.

[03:00] Riley: We support rotation policies; for BYOK the rotation is managed in your KMS. Redwood will honor key versioning and won't retain plaintext key material. We also support envelope encryption with your CMK as the root.

[03:18] Priya: On the controls mapping, we want to see a matrix showing Redwood control names mapped to our Clauses/Controls (ISO 27001 A.7, A.9 etc). What format do you provide?

[03:30] Riley: We typically provide a CSV or spreadsheet with three columns: Redwood control ID, brief description, and customer control mapping. We can include evidence links (redacted) and last tested dates. We'll send a template.

[03:46] Alex: How do you handle data residency? If we restrict data to EU, can you guarantee processing and logs stay in region?

[03:54] Jamie: Yes — for region-bound customers we pin workloads to EU regions and isolate storage. For Hosted customers we have regional endpoints. For Dedicated/Private we can fully ensure egress controls and subnets are constrained. We do need to discuss backup replication though — by default some backups are retained in the same region; cross-region replication is configurable off.

[04:20] Mark: For audit log retention, what granularity and retention windows are available? We need at least seven years for some artifacts.

[04:28] Riley: We support custom retention policies. Default is 90 days in the console, but you can push logs to S3 with lifecycle policies for longer retention. For seven-year retention we recommend exporting to your long-term archival storage (S3 Glacier) via our export connector.

[04:46] Priya: Ok that helps. Also, about SSO — we want SCIM for provisioning and SAML for SSO. Do you support groups mapping to RBAC roles?

[04:56] Jamie: Yes SCIM + SAML are supported. You can map directory groups to Redwood roles (admin, viewer, developer). We can also add custom roles if needed for least-privilege separation.

[05:10] Alex: Any gaps we should be aware of for ISO audits?

[05:14] Riley: The most common gaps customers ask about are evidence exportability and long-term log retention. We've built the trust portal to make evidence access straightforward but sometimes the mapping needs to be tailored. For ISO specifically, we'll supply the Annex A mappings we use and sample procedures.

[05:36] Speaker 1: [overlap] sorry just to clarify, the trust portal is multi-tenant but access is per-tenant?

[05:42] Riley: Correct. The trust portal is tenant-scoped; you only see artifacts for your account.

[05:48] Priya: A couple of practical items: we need an engineering contact to run a short KMS integration test in staging next week, and a controls mapping template.

[05:58] Jamie: Riley will own the KMS test, I'll share the SOC 2 report. We'll also send the controls template.

[06:06] Mark: Also, on network controls — for private deployments, do you support private endpoints with restricted egress? We need to ensure no public internet access from inference nodes.

[06:16] Riley: Yes, private-only endpoints are supported; egress can be locked down to your NATs and VPC endpoints. We also have firewall rules at the host level.

[06:28] Alex: One more thing — our auditors often ask for evidence that key material is not accessible by vendor staff. Is there an attestation we can get?

[06:36] Jamie: We can provide an attestation letter that details key handling practices and that Redwood staff do not have access to customer CMKs. For Dedicated/Private we provide a more technical KMS integration document.

[06:48] Priya: Perfect. Anything else on the audit logs export format? We use JSON events and would like a schema.

[06:56] Riley: We'll share the log schema (fields, event types). The logs include event_type, timestamp, actor, resource, action, outcome, and request_id. We can also include custom fields on request if you forward your correlation ids.

[07:12] Jamie: Alright — to recap: Redwood will send SOC2 Type II redacted report, the controls mapping template, and the log schema. Riley will coordinate the KMS staging test with Mark. Mantle will send their data residency matrix and confirm auditors/roles.

[07:30] Sana: Sounds good. Quick note: prefer documentation links over attachments.

[07:34] Jamie: We'll use the shared drive link.

[07:36] Alex: Thanks — let's schedule the deep dive for next Wednesday.

[07:40] Jamie: I'll follow up with calendar invite and the items. Thanks everyone.
